prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: sideswipe while changing lanes in Pasadena, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported wrist fracture. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1377; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Driver 1 was traveling in the left lane on a multi-lane roadway in Pasadena, Texas, when a sideswipe collision occurred as Driver 2 attempted to change lanes into the same space. Driver 1 reported pain in the wrist and was transported for evaluation. The wrist injury reported by Driver 1 is consistent with the forces expected from a collision of this type. Photographs taken at the scene confirm the general location of the vehicles and some of the reported contact points, and the damage visible on both vehicles matches the described impact. No independent witnesses were located, so the account rests on the statements of the drivers and the physical evidence. Officers and the parties present confirmed that Driver 1 was seated in the vehicle at the time of the collision, and a Passenger was also present in the vehicle. No prior damage to Driver 1's vehicle is known to responding officers or to the owner. Driver 1 is the named driver on the insurance policy covering the vehicle.
